Visioner BIG | 🇺🇦 🇨🇳 🇷🇺 ‼️ ‼️ Former Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba has warned that China could eventually turn against Russia and revive historical territorial claims in the Russian Far East after resolving the Taiwan issue. Kuleba argued that Russia seized approximately one million square kilometers of territory from China in the 19th century, including the area around present-day Vladivostok. He suggested that Beijing could revisit these historical disputes once its priorities regarding Taiwan have been addressed. His remarks reflect a prediction about China’s future intentions rather than an announced Chinese government policy. Beijing and Moscow formally settled their remaining border disputes through agreements completed in 2008. Kuleba’s warning highlights a potential long-term vulnerability in Russia’s growing dependence on China. Although Moscow and Beijing currently maintain close strategic ties, their relationship is shaped by unequal economic power and historical tensions. A future shift in China’s priorities could create new challenges for Russia, but there is currently no indication that Beijing intends to reopen its settled territorial border with Moscow.
